strings.records.tailscale-four-fixes.title: Tailscale: minimum fixed version 1.104.4 for 4 official advisories
strings.records.tailscale-four-fixes.body: TS-2026-014–017 concern SSH Unix socket forwarding, SSH memory DoS, Serve Unix backends, and HTTP/2 capability confusion. The official bulletin specifies at least 1.104.4. A timing gap in changelog updates remains. Do not equate this with fixes for all 11 Tailworm items.
strings.records.tailscale-four-fixes.action: Verify 1.104.4 or later on production clients and check SSH/Serve usage conditions. To temporarily disable SSH forwarding, set TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 and restart the daemon. Do not include headscale or experimental connectors in the same fix scope.
strings.records.tailscale-four-fixes.time: Continued review of the 10/26 bulletin and 10/27 tag / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review
strings.records.fireblocks-no-fix.title: Fireblocks mpc-lib: still no fix after assessment revision.
strings.records.fireblocks-no-fix.body: CERT VU701544 was revised on the 27th at 14:45 UTC. Descendant shares and chain codes may permit access to ancestor/root shares of the same MPC party, but this is not equivalent to obtaining a complete transfer key exceeding the threshold. Actual theft, amounts, and affected customer counts have not been disclosed.
strings.records.fireblocks-no-fix.action: Treat the fix as unavailable, protect chain codes as secrets, and investigate the entire hierarchy. Do not reuse Agent2.4.4 / SDK2.19.1 from the separate eMudhra incident as fixed versions for this vulnerability.
strings.records.fireblocks-no-fix.time: Revised 10/27 23:45 JST / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review
strings.records.fortinet-fips.title: Fortinet FIPS: 7.4 remediation build and inconsistent 7.2 notation
strings.records.fortinet-fips.body: The technical article dated the 27 announces availability of FIPS hardening builds. For 7.4, this is FIPS-CC-74-15 b9481. For 7.2, b9883 in the text differs from b9893 in the download path. Extended support for 7.0FIPS has ended, with no build planned this time.
strings.records.fortinet-fips.action: Match models and builds against official ReadMe files and support downloads. Do not automatically apply an ambiguous 7.2 number. Do not reuse the GA hardening table as individual minimum fixed versions for an unretrieved PSIRT advisory.
strings.records.fortinet-fips.time: 10/27 official update / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review
strings.records.litellm-supplychain-response.tit: LiteLLM: revoke keys and rebuild environments after distribution-path compromise.
strings.records.litellm-supplychain-response.bod: Actual distribution of malicious 1.107.0 and containers was confirmed in the 10/21 incident. The attack-chain report on the 23rd explains the path from an unrevoked master key to publisher tokens and other access. Do not reuse victim counts from the separate March (month 3) incident here.
strings.records.litellm-supplychain-response.act: Check installation and execution paths during the affected period. Before simply updating pip packages, isolate and rebuild the environment and revoke/replace keys that were reachable. Product GHSA fixed versions in this window are separate from post-compromise safety checks.
strings.records.litellm-supplychain-response.tim: Continuing response to the 10/21 incident and 10/23 analysis / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review
strings.records.malware-packages.title: Malicious packages: separately check 27 GHSA malware-category advisories
strings.records.malware-packages.body: Includes trajmetrics0.5.3, numprint1.2.0, and @azure-growth/signup-ux-components1.2.2/1.2.3. Ranges below are as specified in GitHub advisories. Do not infer that all legitimate packages with similar names were compromised. Do not count 27 advisories as 27 newly affected organizations.
strings.records.malware-packages.action: Compare lockfiles and SBOMs with retrieval caches; do not verify suspicious artifacts by executing them. If installed or executed, isolate and rebuild the environment and revoke credentials that were reachable. Do not interpret an unspecified fixed version as meaning a safe version exists or that upgrading alone resolves the issue.
strings.records.malware-packages.time: Current GHSA publication window / malware classification / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review
strings.records.kev-linux-esx.title: KEV: Linux privilege escalation and missing ESX logging added
strings.records.kev-linux-esx.body: KEV version 2026.10.28 contains 1,762 entries. CVE-2026-46300 describes chaining with the 2 PHP flaws; forensicTriage is Yes and the deadline is 10/31. CVE-2026-41709 concerns actions left unlogged after administrator access, with a deadline of 11/11. Addition dates are not attack start dates; deadlines are requirements for US federal agencies.
strings.records.kev-linux-esx.action: Check kernel and embedded-product updates, including the running version after restart. Use the ESX vendor response matrix and treat missing logs as an investigation limitation.
strings.records.php-kernel-identity.title: From PHP to the kernel and identity systems: observed artifacts and uncertainty
strings.records.php-kernel-identity.body: Dream’s report dated 10/26 describes artifacts of PHP2Shell chained with CVE-2026-46300 to gain root on 25 servers: 24 firewalls and an additional management server. It reports decrypted LDAP credentials and enumeration, but explicitly cannot determine whether password spraying, backdoor account creation or SAML key extraction succeeded. These are researcher observations without independent victim confirmation; direct evidence of AI code generation is also absent.
strings.records.php-kernel-identity.action: Restrict exposed management interfaces and update. Where compromise is suspected, investigate management servers, LDAP credentials, tunnels and identity logs. Do not infer undisclosed product names or affected versions.
strings.records.sonet-disclosure.title: So-net: member information and some email passwords exposed
strings.records.sonet-disclosure.body: The official 10/27 notice says access on 10/19 was detected on 23 and disclosure established on 24. It separately reports 2,141,986 So-net member records and 443,495 plala (S course) member records. Passwords for member records are distinct from email passwords in some mail services: the latter were exposed and reset on 27. The notice also reports 16 bank-account records and 7 notification records. Do not add these as a count of people.
strings.records.sonet-disclosure.action: Reset affected email passwords using the official guidance and change reused passwords elsewhere. Do not infer exposure in other services such as NURO.
strings.records.unm-recovery.title: UNM Health: clinical and academic recovery, with a warning about follow-on scams
strings.records.unm-recovery.body: The official 10/28 update reports fully functional clinical operations and resumed classes and research. Ambulance diversion and interrupted outpatient surgery and appointments on 10/26 remain recorded as real impacts. The institution says some end-user devices were affected without penetration of core systems or servers. Attacker claims of stolen data or payment offers are not confirmed disclosure or compensation.
strings.records.unm-recovery.action: Use official hospital channels to check rescheduled appointments. Do not engage with purported attackers or compensation offers.
strings.records.silent-train.title: Silent Train: long-term monitoring of infrastructure serving communications, government and transport
strings.records.silent-train.body: Lumen Black Lotus Labs describes ephemeral relay chains tracked since 2023 and operations targeting management infrastructure. Victim notifications cover multiple years, rather than incidents newly occurring in this review. The report lists communications, government, defense, universities, water, energy and transport among targeted sectors without providing individual outage durations or financial losses.
strings.records.silent-train.action: Review exposed management interfaces, devices usable as relays and management-network telemetry. Do not rely solely on IP reputation.
strings.records.yamaha-nwr100.title: Yamaha NWR100: unauthenticated command execution and CONFIG access
strings.records.yamaha-nwr100.body: CVE-2026-97854 allows unauthenticated OS command execution, scored 9.8 in CVSS v3.1 and 9.3 in v4.0. CVE-2026-109822 concerns unauthenticated access to generated CONFIG files. Rev.26.00.07 and earlier are affected; Rev.26.00.08 is fixed. Potential impact is not a count of actual compromises.
strings.records.yamaha-nwr100.action: Update firmware. If delayed, restrict devices and source IP addresses allowed to access the Web GUI.
strings.records.yamaha-windows.title: Yamaha Windows products: separate installer and service-path fixes
strings.records.yamaha-windows.body: LAN Monitor installers through Ver.1.9.3 have a DLL-loading issue, fixed in Ver.1.10.1; already installed software itself is unaffected by this installer issue. YMS-VPN8 / YMS-VPN8-CP through Ver.1.04.00 have unquoted service paths, fixed in Ver.1.07.00. The latter requires permission to write to the system drive.
strings.records.yamaha-windows.action: Use the official fixed releases and avoid running installers beside untrusted DLLs. Review shared Windows access and write permissions.
strings.records.struts-anysetter.title: Struts REST: any-setter requires configuration as well as an update
strings.records.struts-anysetter.body: In Struts 2 versions 7.2.1–7.3.0, @StrutsParameter restrictions do not cover REST @JsonAnySetter members. JVN advises updating to 7.4.0 or later and using struts.rest.anySetter.requireAnnotations=true with @StrutsParameter(allowDynamicKeys = true). Conditions include REST use and any-setter declarations; this does not establish compromise of all Struts applications.
strings.records.struts-anysetter.action: Check the update, configuration and annotations together. Work around the issue by avoiding any-setter or validating values in the application before storage.
strings.records.edk2-pxe.title: EDK II: distinguish PXE exposure from shipped firmware fixes
strings.records.edk2-pxe.body: The official CVE-2026-97631 advisory describes pre-OS memory corruption by an attacker able to deliver ICMP errors during PXE boot. It identifies master as of 2026-09-14 and still lists Not patched currently. A fix PR does not prove a manufacturer has shipped a corrected BIOS or UEFI release.
strings.records.edk2-pxe.action: Disable unnecessary network boot and restrict PXE paths. Check firmware releases and deployment with the hardware supplier.

records.title: KEV: Linux privilege escalation and missing ESX logging added
records.body: KEV version 2026.10.28 contains 1,762 entries. CVE-2026-46300 describes chaining with the 2 PHP flaws; forensicTriage is Yes and the deadline is 10/31. CVE-2026-41709 concerns actions left unlogged after administrator access, with a deadline of 11/11. Addition dates are not attack start dates; deadlines are requirements for US federal agencies.
records.action: Check kernel and embedded-product updates, including the running version after restart. Use the ESX vendor response matrix and treat missing logs as an investigation limitation.

records.title: From PHP to the kernel and identity systems: observed artifacts and uncertainty
records.body: Dream’s report dated 10/26 describes artifacts of PHP2Shell chained with CVE-2026-46300 to gain root on 25 servers: 24 firewalls and an additional management server. It reports decrypted LDAP credentials and enumeration, but explicitly cannot determine whether password spraying, backdoor account creation or SAML key extraction succeeded. These are researcher observations without independent victim confirmation; direct evidence of AI code generation is also absent.
records.action: Restrict exposed management interfaces and update. Where compromise is suspected, investigate management servers, LDAP credentials, tunnels and identity logs. Do not infer undisclosed product names or affected versions.

records.title: So-net: member information and some email passwords exposed
records.body: The official 10/27 notice says access on 10/19 was detected on 23 and disclosure established on 24. It separately reports 2,141,986 So-net member records and 443,495 plala (S course) member records. Passwords for member records are distinct from email passwords in some mail services: the latter were exposed and reset on 27. The notice also reports 16 bank-account records and 7 notification records. Do not add these as a count of people.
records.action: Reset affected email passwords using the official guidance and change reused passwords elsewhere. Do not infer exposure in other services such as NURO.

records.title: UNM Health: clinical and academic recovery, with a warning about follow-on scams
records.body: The official 10/28 update reports fully functional clinical operations and resumed classes and research. Ambulance diversion and interrupted outpatient surgery and appointments on 10/26 remain recorded as real impacts. The institution says some end-user devices were affected without penetration of core systems or servers. Attacker claims of stolen data or payment offers are not confirmed disclosure or compensation.
records.action: Use official hospital channels to check rescheduled appointments. Do not engage with purported attackers or compensation offers.

records.title: Silent Train: long-term monitoring of infrastructure serving communications, government and transport
records.body: Lumen Black Lotus Labs describes ephemeral relay chains tracked since 2023 and operations targeting management infrastructure. Victim notifications cover multiple years, rather than incidents newly occurring in this review. The report lists communications, government, defense, universities, water, energy and transport among targeted sectors without providing individual outage durations or financial losses.
records.action: Review exposed management interfaces, devices usable as relays and management-network telemetry. Do not rely solely on IP reputation.
records.time: 2026-10-28 / publication time unconfirmed

records.title: Yamaha NWR100: unauthenticated command execution and CONFIG access
records.body: CVE-2026-97854 allows unauthenticated OS command execution, scored 9.8 in CVSS v3.1 and 9.3 in v4.0. CVE-2026-109822 concerns unauthenticated access to generated CONFIG files. Rev.26.00.07 and earlier are affected; Rev.26.00.08 is fixed. Potential impact is not a count of actual compromises.

records.title: Yamaha Windows products: separate installer and service-path fixes
records.body: LAN Monitor installers through Ver.1.9.3 have a DLL-loading issue, fixed in Ver.1.10.1; already installed software itself is unaffected by this installer issue. YMS-VPN8 / YMS-VPN8-CP through Ver.1.04.00 have unquoted service paths, fixed in Ver.1.07.00. The latter requires permission to write to the system drive.
records.action: Use the official fixed releases and avoid running installers beside untrusted DLLs. Review shared Windows access and write permissions.

records.title: Struts REST: any-setter requires configuration as well as an update
records.body: In Struts 2 versions 7.2.1–7.3.0, @StrutsParameter restrictions do not cover REST @JsonAnySetter members. JVN advises updating to 7.4.0 or later and using struts.rest.anySetter.requireAnnotations=true with @StrutsParameter(allowDynamicKeys = true). Conditions include REST use and any-setter declarations; this does not establish compromise of all Struts applications.
records.action: Check the update, configuration and annotations together. Work around the issue by avoiding any-setter or validating values in the application before storage.

records.title: EDK II: distinguish PXE exposure from shipped firmware fixes
records.body: The official CVE-2026-97631 advisory describes pre-OS memory corruption by an attacker able to deliver ICMP errors during PXE boot. It identifies master as of 2026-09-14 and still lists Not patched currently. A fix PR does not prove a manufacturer has shipped a corrected BIOS or UEFI release.
records.action: Disable unnecessary network boot and restrict PXE paths. Check firmware releases and deployment with the hardware supplier.
